evals.name: Analyze a .NET MVC project and make wireframes
evals.prompt: Here's my ASP.NET MVC project. Document it and make wireframes for the main screens.
expectations: Runs or emulates analyze_project.py and writes blueprint/profile.json that follows the profile schema
Wireframe spec screen ids match the screens found in Views/ (for example account-login, books-index) and the shared layout is not treated as a screen
Renders SVG files with render_wireframe.py and they open without errors
Labels inferences as ASSUMPTION: or inferred, and does not read or copy anything from the .env file
Ends with a short summary and list of files instead of pasting the files into chat

evals.name: Idea only, interview path
evals.prompt: I want to build an app that helps freelancers track unpaid invoices and send reminders. I have no code yet. Help me plan it.
expectations: Does not try to run the analyzer on a codebase (there is none)
Asks a short interview of at most 5 questions in one message, about users, platform, must-have features, constraints and data or integrations
After the answers, or on stated defaults, writes blueprint/profile.json with project.status idea and confidence.overall low
Every detail that came from the interview or from guessing is marked ASSUMPTION:
Does not invent technical details such as a framework or database without labeling them as assumptions

evals.name: Wireframes for a mobile app
evals.prompt: Make wireframes for a mobile habit tracker app: login, a daily checklist, a streak screen, and settings.
expectations: Writes a wireframe spec JSON with screens for login, the daily checklist, the streak view and settings, using the mobile viewport
Every screen except the first is reachable through navigates_to, and each screen has at most one primary button
Renders SVGs with render_wireframe.py and also produces a screen-flow Mermaid diagram that passes validate_mermaid.py
Uses realistic labels (habit names, streak counts) and no filler text
Adds empty or error variants for the screen that loads data, named with the double-hyphen pattern such as daily-checklist--empty

evals.name: Flowchart of the auth flow
evals.prompt: Draw a flowchart of the sign-in and registration flow of this app.
expectations: Bases the flow on the real routes and screens (POST /account/login, POST /account/register, account-login, account-register)
Outputs a Mermaid flowchart in a fenced block and validate_mermaid.py exits 0
Notices or states that the login handler does not verify credentials, or labels the credential check as an assumption
Node ids and names come from the profile and are not renamed

evals.name: Three-sprint plan with dependencies
evals.prompt: Break this project into a 3-sprint plan. I work alone. Include estimates and dependencies.
expectations: Writes blueprint/sprints/sprint-plan.md with the required table header (ID, Epic, Story, Points, Priority, Depends On, Sprint, Acceptance Criteria)
Uses only the points 1, 2, 3, 5 or 8, and no story depends on a story in a later sprint
Sprint 1 is a thin vertical slice that can be demonstrated end to end
export_sprint.py exits 0 and produces the CSV and JSON files
States the capacity assumption for a solo developer instead of asking about team size

evals.name: PRD from a README
evals.prompt: Turn this README into a PRD I can show my team.
expectations: Writes blueprint/requirements/prd.md with the sections problem, goals and non-goals, personas, scope (MVP vs later), functional requirements, non-functional requirements, success metrics, open questions and risks
Functional requirements are numbered FR-001, FR-002 and so on, each with a priority
Requirements trace to the README: the planned features appear, and the not-planned items (maps, payments, native apps) are in non-goals or later scope
Does not invent numeric success metrics as facts; they are marked ASSUMPTION: or listed as open questions
Also writes blueprint/profile.json with status idea and starts the markdown file with the generated-by header

evals.name: Vague prompt that should still trigger
evals.prompt: I have a rough idea for an app but I'm stuck. Help me figure out what to build first.
expectations: Recognizes this as a planning request and uses the project-blueprint workflow
Asks at most 3 clarifying questions, or 5 in a single idea-only interview message, and does not interrogate the user over several turns
Works toward an MVP scope (must-have features, a first sprint or slice) rather than generic advice
Marks anything it guessed as ASSUMPTION: and offers the other artifacts (wireframes, user stories, sprint plan) as next steps

evals.name: Negative case: fix a bug
evals.prompt: Fix this null reference bug. In BooksController.Details, `return View(_db.Books.Find(id));` throws a NullReferenceException in the view when the id does not exist. What should I change?
expectations: Does not use the project-blueprint skill and does not create a blueprint/ folder
Does not run analyze_project.py, render_wireframe.py, validate_mermaid.py or export_sprint.py
Explains the cause (Find returns null for a missing id) and gives a concrete code fix such as returning NotFound() when the book is null
Keeps the answer focused on the bug and does not produce wireframes, diagrams, stories or sprint plans
